questions.question: The _____ is the extended margin of each continent occupied by relatively shallow seas and gulfs.
questions.questionHtml: The _____ is the extended margin of each continent occupied by relatively shallow seas and gulfs.
questions.solution: The continental shelf is the extended margin of each continent occupied by relatively shallow seas and gulfs. The Continental Shelf of all oceans together covers 7.5% of the total area of the oceans.  The gradient of continental is 1° or even less.

questions.question: The percentage of earth's water found in the oceans is ______.
questions.questionHtml: The percentage of earth's water found in the oceans is ______.
questions.solution: The oceans contain 97.3% of the water on Earth, while freshwater sources such as lakes, rivers, and groundwater make up less than 1% of the total water supply.

questions.question: Normally, there is a ________ day interval between spring tides and neap tides.
questions.questionHtml: Normally, there is a ________ day interval between spring tides and neap tides.
questions.solution: There is a seven-day interval between the spring tides and neap tides. Tides are the rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined effects of the gravitational forces exerted by the Moon and the Sun, and the rotation of the Earth.

questions.question: Due to attraction of the sun and the moon, what is the frequency of up and falls down of ocean water in a day?
questions.questionHtml: Due to attraction of the sun and the moon, what is the frequency of up and falls down of ocean water in a day?
questions.solution: Due to attraction of the sun and the moon, the frequency of up and falls down of ocean water in a day is two. The gravitational attraction between the Earth, the Moon, and the Sun causes tides in the Earth's oceans.

questions.question: The salinity of ocean waters is calculated as the amount of salt (in gm) dissolved in _____ gm of seawater.
questions.questionHtml: The salinity of ocean waters is calculated as the amount of salt (in gm) dissolved in _____ gm of seawater.
questions.solution: Salinity is the total dissolved salts in seawater, calculated as the amount of salt in 1,000 gm of seawater. The average ocean salinity is 35 parts per thousand, while the Dead Sea's salinity is approximately 340 gm per liter. Factors affecting salinity include evaporation, precipitation, river inflow, freezing/thawing, wind, and ocean currents.

questions.question: Madagascar is located in the ______ Ocean.
questions.questionHtml: Madagascar is located in the ______ Ocean.
questions.solution: Madagascar is an island country in the Indian Ocean. Madagascar is the largest African island situated in the Indian Ocean, about 450 km (280 mi) east of the coast of Mozambique. The fourth-largest island in the world has been isolated for about 88 million years and many of its plants and animals are unique to the island.

questions.question: With which of the following oceans would you associate the ‘Ring of Fire’?
questions.questionHtml: With which of the following oceans would you associate the ‘Ring of Fire’?
questions.solution: The Ring of Fire is associated with the Pacific Ocean. It is a horseshoe-shaped zone of high volcanic activity and frequent earthquakes caused by plate tectonics. Spanning 40,000 km, it includes the Pacific coasts of the Americas and parts of the western Pacific.

questions.question: Approximately how much percentage (nearest to integer) of total water on the surface of earth is accounted for by the oceans?
questions.questionHtml: Approximately how much percentage (nearest to integer) of total water on the surface of earth is accounted for by the oceans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 97.

Important Points

  • 97 percent (nearest to integer) of the total water on the surface of the earth is accounted for by the oceans.
  • Earth is called the "Blue Planet" because it looks blue from space due to the presence of water on its surface.
  • Around 71% of the Earth's surface is covered with water.
  • While the other 29% consists of continents and islands.

Additional Information

  • Total water on earth is majorly divided into two parts:
    • Freshwater (2.5%)
    • Saline water (97.4%)
  • Freshwater is again divided into four parts:
    • Icecaps and glaciers (68.7%)
    • Groundwater (30.1%)
    • Surface water (0.3%) (lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, etc.)
    • Others (0.9%) (soil moisture, atmospheric moisture, etc.)

options.text: Pacific Ocean > Antarctic Ocean > Indian Ocean > Atlantic Ocean

options.html: Pacific Ocean > Indian Ocean > Atlantic Ocean > Antarctic Ocean

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pacific Ocean > Atlantic Ocean > Indian Ocean > Antarctic Ocean.
Key Points
  • The correct sequence of oceans according to size (from largest to smallest) Pacific Ocean > Atlantic Ocean > Indian Ocean > Antarctic Ocean.

Additional Information Pacific Ocean

  • The largest ocean on Earth is the Pacific Ocean.
  • It is the largest of the world's oceans, covering an area of about 63.8 million square miles (165.25 million square kilometers), which is roughly one-third of the Earth's total surface area.
  • The Pacific Ocean lies between the continents of Asia and Australia on the west and North America and South America on the east., and it is also the deepest ocean in the world.

​Atlantic Ocean

  • The Atlantic Ocean is the second-largest of the world's five oceans, with an area of about 106,460,000 km².
  • It covers approximately 20% of Earth's surface and about 29% of its water surface area.
  • the Atlantic drives our weather patterns, including hurricanes, and is home to many species from sea turtles to dolphins. For centuries the Atlantic Ocean has been a key avenue of trade and travel.
  • The ocean's name, derived from Greek mythology, means the "Sea of Atlas." The oldest known mention of this name is contained in The Histories of Herodotus around 450 BC.

​Indian Ocean

  • The Indian Ocean is the third-largest in the world. 
  • The Java Trench is the deepest point in the Indian Ocean.
  • It makes up approximately 20% of the Earth's water surface. 

Arctic Ocean

  • The Arctic Ocean is the smallest ocean.
  • It is located within the Arctic Circle and surrounds the North Pole.
  • It is connected with the Pacific Ocean by a narrow stretch of shallow water known as the Bering Strait.
  • It is surrounded by the northern coasts of North America and Eurasia.
  • It is completely covered with ice for the majority of the year.

questions.question: In the context of water bodies, Neap Tides occur:
questions.questionHtml: In the context of water bodies, Neap Tides occur:

options.text: when the earth, moon and sun line up in a straight line
options.html: when the earth, moon and sun line up in a straight line

options.text: when the sun and moon are on the opposite sides
options.html: when the sun and moon are on the opposite sides

options.text: when there is so much interference by continents
options.html: when there is so much interference by continents

options.text: when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other
options.html: when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other

questions.solution: Neap tides occur when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other, resulting in the least difference between high and low tide levels, making them weaker than spring tides. They happen during the first and third quarters of the moon. Neap tides feature reduced tidal ranges as the sun's gravitational pull partially cancels out the moon's. In contrast, spring tides occur when the Earth, moon, and sun align, producing the highest high tides and lowest low tides, due to the combined gravitational forces. The moon's proximity to Earth gives its gravitational force a more significant impact on tides.

questions.question: What is the salinity of the Dead Sea (per litre of water)?
questions.questionHtml: What is the salinity of the Dead Sea (per litre of water)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 340 grams.

Key Points

  • The Dead Sea is known for its extreme salinity, which makes it one of the saltiest bodies of water in the world.
  • The salinity of the Dead Sea is approximately 340 grams of salt per litre of water.
  • This high salt concentration is due to the high evaporation rates and the lack of outlets for the water to flow out.
  • Due to its high salinity, the Dead Sea is unable to support marine life, which is why it is called the "Dead" Sea.

Additional Information

  • Salinity: Salinity refers to the concentration of dissolved salts in water. It is usually measured in grams of salt per litre of water or parts per thousand (ppt).
  • Evaporation: Evaporation is the process by which water is transformed from liquid to gas. High evaporation rates in the Dead Sea region lead to an increase in the concentration of salts.
  • Dead Sea: The Dead Sea is a salt lake bordered by Jordan to the east and Israel and Palestine to the west. Its surface and shores are 430.5 meters below sea level, making it the Earth's lowest elevation on land.
  • Marine Life: Due to its high salinity, the Dead Sea cannot support fish and other aquatic life. Only some types of bacteria and microbial fungi can survive in such a salty environment.

questions.question: The rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water twice in a day is called ______.
questions.questionHtml: The rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water twice in a day is called ______.

questions.question: El Nino is a name given to the periodic development of a warm ocean current along the coast of _______.
questions.questionHtml: El Nino is a name given to the periodic development of a warm ocean current along the coast of _______.

It is caused by the warming of surface waters in the tropical Pacific and affects Indian storms and agriculture. Other ocean currents mentioned include the Gulf Stream, West Wind, Peru Current, and West Australian Current.

questions.question: In the context of mapping climate data, what term refers to a line drawn through all points on a map that contain the same amount of cloud?
questions.questionHtml: In the context of mapping climate data, what term refers to a line drawn through all points on a map that contain the same amount of cloud?
questions.solution:
Key Points

  • Isoneph:-
    • It refers to a line drawn through all points on a map that contain the same amount of cloud.
    • It is a type of isoline, which is a line that connects points of equal value.
    • Other common isolines include contour lines (elevation), isobars (atmospheric pressure), and isotherms (temperature).
    • Isonephs are used by meteorologists and climatologists to visualize the distribution of cloud cover over a region.
    • They can be used to identify areas of high and low cloud cover, as well as to track the movement of clouds over time.

Additional Information

  • Isohels:-
    • These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal sunshine duration.
  • Isocheims:-
    • These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal temperature.
  • Isochalaz:-
    • These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal hail size.

questions.solution: Ocean currents are the streams of water flowing constantly on the ocean surface in definite directions. They are driven by various factors such as wind, temperature, salinity, and the rotation of the earth.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about tides is INCORRECT ?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements about tides is INCORRECT?

options.text: High tides occur when the moon is in its first and last quarter.
options.html: High tides occur when the moon is in its first and last quarter.

options.text: Low tides are also called neap tides.
options.html: Low tides are also called neap tides.

options.text: Tides are caused by the gravitational pull exerted by the sun and the moon on Earth's surface.
options.html: Tides are caused by the gravitational pull exerted by the sun and the moon on Earth's surface.

options.text: Spring tides occur on full moon and new moon days.
options.html: Spring tides occur on full moon and new moon days.

questions.solution: Tides are caused by the gravitational forces of the Moon and the Sun and the rotation of the Earth. There are two types of tides: spring tides and neap tides. Spring tides occur when the Sun, Moon, and Earth are in a straight line, resulting in higher tide levels. They occur twice a month during the full and new moon periods. Neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon are at right angles to each other, and their gravitational forces tend to counteract each other. The Moon's attraction, though more than twice as strong as the Sun's, is diminished by the counteracting force of the Sun's gravitational pull. Neap tides also occur twice a month, with a seven-day interval between them and spring tides. Therefore, the correct answer is that high tides occur during the first and last quarter of the Moon.

questions.question: The South China Sea is a part of which of the following oceans?

The correct answer is Pacific Ocean

  • The South China Sea is a significant body of water for international trade, with major shipping routes passing through it.

It is rich in marine life and resources like oil and gas. It lies before the continental slope, which marks a steep boundary leading to deeper oceanic regions.

Shallow earthquakes and volcanic activity are common. Examples include mid-ocean ridges like the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, characterized by seafloor spreading and ocean basin expansion.

questions.question: Where is the deepest point on earth, the Mariana Trench, located?
questions.questionHtml: Where is the deepest point on earth, the Mariana Trench, located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pacific Ocean.
Key Points

  • The Mariana Trench, which is the deepest point on earth, is located in the Pacific Ocean.
  • It is situated in the western Pacific Ocean, to the east of the Mariana Islands.
  • The Mariana Trench is approximately 2,550 km long and 69 km wide, with a depth of 10,994 meters at its deepest point, known as the Challenger Deep.
  • The trench is formed by the collision of the Pacific Plate and the Philippine Plate, which creates a subduction zone and leads to the formation of the deepest part of the ocean floor.

Additional Information

 

  • Atlantic Ocean -
    • This is incorrect because the Atlantic Ocean, while vast and home to significant depths, does not contain the deepest point on Earth.
    • Its deepest point is the Milwaukee Deep (Puerto Rico Trench), which is approximately 8,376 meters (27,480 feet) deep, far shallower compared to the Mariana Trench.
  • Indian Ocean -
    • This option is not correct. The Indian Ocean's deepest point is the Java Trench (also known as the Sunda Trench), with a maximum depth of about 7,725 meters (25,344 feet), making it much shallower than the Mariana Trench.
  • Arctic Ocean -
    • This is also incorrect. The Arctic Ocean's deepest point is the Molloy Deep in the Fram Strait, with a depth of about 5,550 meters (18,209 feet).
    • While fascinating for its own ecological and geographical characteristics, it does not compare to the depth of the Mariana Trench.

 

Thus, the Mariana Trench's extreme depth and unique ecosystem have made it a subject of much scientific research and interest, emphasizing its significance located in the Pacific Ocean.

Hence, The correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: Identify the odd option in relation to the oceanic layers.
questions.questionHtml: Identify the odd option in relation to the oceanic layers.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is The Oceanic Slope.

Key Points

  •  Scientists have divided the ocean into five main layers. These layers, known as "zones", extend from the surface to the most extreme depths.
    • Epipelagic Zone - It extends from the surface to 200 meters (656 feet).
    • Mesopelagic Zone - Below the epipelagic zone is the mesopelagic zone, extending from 200 meters (656 feet) to 1,000 meters (3,281 feet).
    • Bathypelagic Zone - This zone extends from 1,000 meters (3,281 feet) down to 4,000 meters (13,124 feet).
    • Abyssopelagic Zone - It extends from 4,000 meters (13,124 feet) to 6,000 meters (19,686 feet).
    • Hadalpelagic Zone - This layer extends from 6,000 meters (19,686 feet) to the bottom of the deepest parts of the ocean.

Additional Information

  • The ocean deeps are the deepest part of the ocean. They are long, narrow, steep-sided and flat-floored depressions on the ocean floor.
  • A continental shelf is a portion of a continent that is submerged under an area of relatively shallow water known as a shelf sea. 
  • The continuously sloping portion of the continental margin, seaward of the continental shelf and extending down to the deep sea floor of the abyssal plain, is known as the continental slope. It is characterised by gradients of 2.5 degrees. It extends between the depth of 180 to 3600 metres.

questions.question: The thermocline layer is the _______ layer of the ocean.
questions.questionHtml: The thermocline layer is the _______ layer of the ocean.
questions.solution: The thermocline layer is the second layer of the ocean, situated between the mixed layer at the surface and the deep water layer. It is characterized by a rapid change in temperature with depth, acting as a barrier to the mixing of surface water and deep water. The mixed layer is the topmost layer, influenced by wind and waves, while the deep water layer lies below the thermocline with a more gradual temperature decrease. The thermocline is crucial for ocean dynamics, marine life distribution, and climate studies due to its role in heat distribution and ocean circulation.

questions.question: What is the average temperature usually in the hills of the western Ghats?
questions.questionHtml: What is the average temperature usually in the hills of the western Ghats?
questions.solution: The average annual temperature hovers around 15°C (59 °F) in the region. Frost is common in some parts, with temperatures dropping to freezing during winter.

questions.question: Identify a factor that does NOT determine the temperature of ocean waters.
questions.questionHtml: Identify a factor that does NOT determine the temperature of ocean waters.

options.text: Unequal distribution of land and water
options.html: Unequal distribution of land and water

questions.solution: Longitude does not influence the temperature of ocean waters, unlike factors such as unequal distribution of land and water, latitude, and ocean currents. Latitude impacts temperature by determining the sun's angle and daylight duration. Ocean currents transport warm or cold water, affecting local temperatures. The unequal distribution of land and water leads to varying heating and cooling rates due to different heat capacities, influencing adjacent ocean temperatures. Latitude specifies a location's north-south position, while longitude specifies the east-west position but does not affect temperature. Ocean currents are driven by forces like wind, temperature differences, and salinity gradients.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the ocean floor?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a part of the ocean floor?
questions.solution: The deep sea shelf is not a recognized part of the ocean floor. The ocean floor is divided into the continental shelf, continental slope, and deep sea plain (abyssal plain). The continental shelf is the submerged perimeter of continents, the continental slope connects the shelf to the deep ocean floor, and the deep sea plain is a flat area of the deep ocean. Ocean floor features include mid-ocean ridges, seamounts, and trenches. Technological advancements like sonar mapping and submersibles have expanded our knowledge of the ocean floor, which is crucial for understanding geological processes, marine ecosystems, and human impact on oceans.

questions.question: In 1962, who published 'The History of Ocean Basins', which outlined the theory of how tectonic plates could move, later called 'sea floor spreading'?
questions.questionHtml: In 1962, who published 'The History of Ocean Basins', which outlined the theory of how tectonic plates could move, later called 'sea floor spreading'?
questions.solution: Harry Hammond Hess published 'The History of Ocean Basins' in 1962, introducing the theory of sea floor spreading, which explained the movement of tectonic plates. This theory provided a mechanism for Alfred Wegener's earlier hypothesis of continental drift. Hess's work was crucial in understanding the formation of mid-ocean ridges and the symmetrical magnetic patterns on the ocean floor. Sea floor spreading is a fundamental aspect of plate tectonics, which describes the movement of Earth's lithosphere. Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912, while Louis Bauer and George Edward Backus contributed to other geophysical fields.

questions.question: What is the average salinity of the Indian ocean?
questions.questionHtml: What is the average salinity of the Indian ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​35 o/oo.

Key Points

  • The common range of ocean salinity ranges between 33-37 grams per liter (33 - 37%).
  • In sea water, there are commonly 35 grams of dissolved salts in each liter.
  • The salinity in the Indian Ocean is in the middle of 32 and 37 percent.
  • The highest level of salinity is in the Arabian Sea and along a belt of water situated between southern Africa and southwestern Australia.

Additional Information

  • ​The Atlantic Ocean has the most excessive salinity of the five oceans. 
  • The slightest saline ocean, by comparison, is the Arctic Ocean, which has a normal salinity of 28–30 g/kg owing to the low rate of evaporation and meltwater from the ice-caps.
  • Ocean salt firstly comes from rocks on land and openings in the seafloor.

questions.question: Which is the deepest point of Earth's oceans with a depth of 11,022 metres?
questions.questionHtml: Which is the deepest point of Earth's oceans with a depth of 11,022 metres?
questions.solution: The Mariana Trench, located in the Pacific Ocean, is the deepest point on Earth with a depth of 10,994 meters at Challenger Deep. It lies to the east of the Mariana Islands and is formed by the subduction of the Pacific Plate beneath the Philippine Plate. The Atlantic Ocean's deepest point is the Milwaukee Deep in the Puerto Rico Trench at 8,376 meters, the Indian Ocean's deepest is the Java Trench at 7,725 meters, and the Arctic Ocean's deepest is the Molloy Deep at 5,550 meters, all significantly shallower than the Mariana Trench.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a force that influences ocean currents?

questions.solution:
• Magnetic fields of the earth deflect most of the solar wind and have no effect on ocean currents.
  • Ocean currents have influences of Coriolis force, frictional force, and heating effect of the sun.

questions.question: How much percentage of Earth's water make up the oceans?
questions.questionHtml: How much percentage of Earth's water make up the oceans?
questions.solution: The oceans hold 97% of Earth's water, making them the largest water reservoir, covering about 71% of the planet's surface. This saline water contains around 3.5% salt, rendering it unsuitable for drinking or irrigation without desalination. Only 3% of Earth's water is freshwater, found in glaciers, ice caps, groundwater, lakes, rivers, and the atmosphere. Freshwater, vital for human consumption and agriculture, constitutes a mere 2.5-2.75% of the total water on Earth. Desalination and efficient water usage are essential to address water scarcity, with climate change and global warming affecting freshwater distribution and availability.

questions.question: Labrador Sea and Mediterranean Sea are part of the:
questions.questionHtml: Labrador Sea and Mediterranean Sea are part of the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Atlantic Ocean.Key Points

  • The Labrador sea is a part of the North Atlantic Ocean.
    • The Atlantic Ocean is the second-largest ocean of the world.
    • The Labrador sea is between the Labrador Peninsula and Greenland.
    • It is connected with Baffin Bay in the north through the Davis Strait and with Hudson Bay in the west through Hudson Strait.
    • It contains one of the world's largest turbidity current channel systems, the Northwest Atlantic Mid-Ocean Channel.
  • The Mediterranean Sea is an intercontinental sea that stretches from the Atlantic Ocean on the west to Asia on the east and separates Europe from Africa.
    • Calypso Deep, located in the Hellenic Trench, Ionian Sea southwest of Pylos, Greece, is the deepest part of the Mediterranean Sea, with a maximum depth of 5,267 m.
    • The Mediterranean Sea extends for about 4,000 km (west to east) from the Strait of Gibraltar to the Gulf of Iskenderun on Turkey's southwestern coast.

questions.question: Which water body surrounds India in the west?
questions.questionHtml: Which water body surrounds India in the west?
questions.solution: The Arabian Sea is a region of the northern Indian Ocean bounded on the north by Pakistan and Iran, on the west by the Gulf of Aden, Guardafui Channel and the Arabian Peninsula, and on the east by India. It is the water body that surrounds India in the west.

questions.question: What is the shallowest part of an ocean showing an average gradient of 1° or even less called?
questions.questionHtml: What is the shallowest part of an ocean showing an average gradient of 1° or even less called?
questions.solution: Continental shelf -​The Continental shelf is a relatively shallow sea and extended part of each continent occupied by the bay.It is the shallowest part of the ocean showing an average gradient of 1° or even less.The shelf usually ends at a very vertical slope, which is called a shelf brake.The width of the continental shelves varies from one ocean to another.

questions.question: The Siberian Shelf, one of the coastal shelves of the Arctic Ocean, is the largest continental shelf on Earth. How many kilometres does it extend offshore?
questions.questionHtml: The Siberian Shelf, one of the coastal shelves of the Arctic Ocean, is the largest continental shelf on Earth. How many kilometres does it extend offshore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1,500 kmKey Points

  • The Siberian Shelf is a coastal shelf in the Arctic Ocean and is the largest continental shelf of the Earth, a part of the continental shelf of Russia
  • It extends from the continent of Eurasia in the general area of North Siberia (hence the name) into the Arctic Ocean.
  • It stretches 1,500 kilometers (930 mi) offshore.
  • The Siberian Shelf is the habitat for numerous flora and fauna.

Additional Information

  • A continental shelf is the edge of a continent that lies under the ocean.
  • Continents are the seven main divisions of land on Earth.
  • A continental shelf extends from the coastline of a continent to a drop-off point called the shelf break.
  • From the break, the shelf descends toward the deep ocean floor in what is called the Continental slope.

questions.question: When the sun, the moon and the earth are in a straight line, the height of the tide will be higher. What are these tides called?
questions.questionHtml: When the sun, the moon and the earth are in a straight line, the height of the tide will be higher. What are these tides called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Spring tides.

Key Points

  • Spring tides occur when the sun, the moon, and the earth are in a straight line during the new moon and full moon phases.
  • These tides are characterized by higher high tides and lower low tides due to the combined gravitational pull of the sun and the moon.
  • The term "spring" does not refer to the season but rather the concept of "springing forth" in terms of increased tidal range.
  • Spring tides happen approximately twice a month, during the full moon and new moon phases.

Additional Information

  • Neap tides:
    • Neap tides occur when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other (first and third quarters of the moon).
    • These tides are characterized by a smaller tidal range, with lower high tides and higher low tides.
    • The gravitational forces of the sun and the moon partially cancel each other out during neap tides.
  • Diurnal tide:
    • Diurnal tides refer to a tidal pattern with one high tide and one low tide each day.
    • This type of tide is less common and typically occurs in certain geographical regions.
    • Diurnal tides are found in areas such as the Gulf of Mexico and parts of Southeast Asia.
  • Gravitational forces:
    • The gravitational pull of the moon and the sun affects the Earth's water, causing tides.
    • The moon has a greater influence on tides due to its proximity to Earth compared to the sun.
    • Tides are the periodic rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined effects of gravitational forces exerted by the moon, the sun, and the rotation of the Earth.
